meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national legal system; Islamic Sharia as principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution; limited administrative court review via the Council of State)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1992)
Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments of the League of Arab States (Unified Arab Investment Agreement)
Egypt-European Union Association Agreement (trade and investment framework)
Agadir Agreement / Pan-Arab Free Trade Area (PAFTA) / African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 8 of 2022; Executive Regulations of Law No. 80 of 2002 and amendments; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended) and its Executive Regulations (UBO filing obligations); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and Executive Regulations (Decree No. 2310 of 2018, as amended); GAFI Beneficial Ownership disclosure directives; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) AML/CFT rules; EMLCU (Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit) instructions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / competent authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Chamber of Commerce in country of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted to the GAFI-authorized incorporation agent, specifying the LLC formation and all sub-delegations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin of the grantor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration form (UBO statement) covering all natural persons ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: LLC founders / authorized signatories, subsequently notarized before an Egyptian Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local notarization (Arabic) for signatures executed in Egypt; Hague Apostille if executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / banker's diligence letter for each non-resident founder and for the newly formed LLC account mandate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank in the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the bank is in a Hague member state) or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized lease contract (Ijara) for the registered office, attested by the Egyptian Real Estate Registry and Tax Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local Egyptian notarization and real estate registration only

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / criminal record extract for each manager resident in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Ministry of Interior (Criminal Records Department) or foreign equivalent for non-resident managers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD screening against Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002 (Articles 2-4, 6, 9), EMLCU regulations, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, HMT/UK sanctions, EU restrictive measures, and domestic Egyptian lists issued by the CBE and the Ministry of Justice. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) required for PEPs, family members, and close associates (FATF Recommendation 12), with ongoing transaction monitoring and source-of-funds verification for non-resident founders; written compliance sign-off by the incorporation agent is required before file submission to GAFI.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI integrated electronic incorporation portal with automatic link to the Egyptian Commercial Registry (Shahr El-Togary) - https://www.gafi.gov.eg; name reservation is processed through the 'Invest in Egypt' digital window and the Commercial Registry name search module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary statutory company name must be in Arabic script and comply with Egyptian commercial naming norms under the Executive Regulations of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; a Latin (English/French) transliteration may be registered as a secondary name. Arabic name must avoid foreign-only or religious-offensive structures and must align with the object clause (e-commerce / hydroponics equipment retail).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words contrary to public order, decency, or Islamic Sharia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The GAFI Commercial Registry issues a reasoned electronic rejection notice. The applicant may file an administrative appeal with the GAFI Legal Affairs Committee within 30 days of rejection, providing a corrected name or written justification where the name was refused for ambiguity or similarity to an existing registered mark. If the Committee rejects again, the applicant may either submit a new name application (after a 15-day moratorium) or challenge the decision before the Council of State (Conseil d'Etat) administrative court. A rejected applicant may also review and rely, with permission, on an advance name clearance for the English transliteration only where the Arabic name must be amended.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in Egypt is mandatory for LLC incorporation; pure virtual-office addresses are not accepted by the Commercial Registry. Serviced office / co-working tenancies with a dedicated physical desk and notarized sublease may satisfy the test, but the lease must be registered with the Real Estate Registry and the Tax Authority, and all statutory books, UBO documentation, and board or manager meeting records must be physically accessible at that office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% probability of unannounced inspection within the first 18 months: GAFI, the Commercial Registry and the Egyptian Tax Authority perform random and complaint-driven physical visits to verify commercial substance, particularly for LLCs with non-resident ownership and online-only sales; inspection risk increases upon tax registration and VAT card issuance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended), Articles 90-102 (Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 2, 5 and 14; Executive Regulations of the Investment Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2316 of 2018); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Consumer Protection Law No. 181 of 2018.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop for Company Incorporation, in coordination with the Commercial Registry and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Certificate Application (Request for Issuance of Company Incorporation Certificate) filed together with the notarized Memorandum of Association (Aqd Al-Ta'sis).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to LLCs under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended; the founders determine the subscribed capital, which must be fully subscribed and fully paid at formation. Cash capital is deposited in a provisional 'company in formation' bank account and evidenced by an official bank capital certificate; in-kind contributions require a licensed valuator's report. No escrow account is statutorily mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation application of the Company, evidenced by the notarized Memorandum of Association filed with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) under Law No. 159 of 1981, is approved and all subscribers' shares are allotted. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the address stated in the Memorandum of Association, and GAFI and the Commercial Registry shall be duly notified. FURTHER RESOLVED that [Name of General Manager] is appointed General Manager and principal signatory for a five-year term, with authority to represent the Company before all authorities and banks and to open and operate Company accounts. RESOLVED FURTHER that incorporation counsel is directed to complete registration, publication, and licensing formalities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) within the Ministry of Finance; electronic tax-services and e-filing portal https://www.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC first obtains a 10-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) through the ETA registration service by submitting the certified incorporation certificate, memorandum of association, commercial registry extract, tax card request form, board/manager authorization, identity documents, and proof of registered address; for VAT/e-invoicing purposes the same TIN is used, after the taxpayer is added to the ETA VAT registry and the e-invoicing/e-receipt platform. Nonresident vendors with no Egyptian establishment but with taxable Egyptian supply must complete the nonresident VAT/e-invoice registration mechanism and obtain an ETA-issued taxpayer identifier before issuing cleared e-invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; an Egyptian LLC is a separate resident taxpayer under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, taxed on worldwide income, while foreign shareholders have no pass-through tax treatment and are subject to withholding on distributions if any.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Egyptian law does not provide a check-the-box election, fiscal unity/group election, or domestic hybrid mismatch election. A single-member LLC is not eligible for disregarded-entity treatment and cannot elect to be taxed as a partnership; treaty-based hybrid mismatch positions are limited by domestic substance rules and the adoption of the BEPS minimum standard.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under Law No. 67 of 2016, implemented by the Egyptian Tax Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies/services is the mandatory VAT registration threshold (voluntary registration is allowed below this); foreign e-commerce sellers making taxable remote supplies to Egyptian buyers may become obliged to register as non-resident VAT payers once the same turnover threshold is reached.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt has a mandatory central e-invoicing and e-receipt system administered by ETA. Registered businesses must clear each electronic invoice/receipt through the ETA integration platform in real time, using official XML/JSON schemas, submit via secure API with digital certificate authentication, and incorporate the ETA-returned unique invoice code and cryptographic QR stamp on the customer-facing document; non-compliance suspends the invoice validity and input VAT deduction rights.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for goods physically exported from Egypt and for certain international/offshore services supplied to nonresidents. The exporter must be a registered VAT person, issue an ETA-cleared tax invoice, supply proof that ownership passed to the nonresident customer, and evidence customs exit of the goods from Egyptian territory; export proceeds must be received through the banking system in freely convertible foreign currency and, when required, repatriated within the Central Bank of Egypt deadline (180-day standard compliance horizon).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (certified or electronic through Egyptian Customs)
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air, for typical cross-border e-commerce fulfilment)
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the Egyptian seller
ETA-cleared e-invoice/tax invoice with valid QR code and UUID
Foreign-trade contract, purchase order and Incoterms evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit notification proving FX proceeds were received in Egypt
Certificate of origin and any export licence/permit applicable to the goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA examination focuses on congruency among the e-invoice, customs declaration, transport documents, and bank FX statements. False or unsupported export zero-rating or refund claims are re-assessed at the standard 14% VAT, the corresponding input VAT is clawed back, late-return/delay surcharges are applied, the taxpayer may be suspended from the e-invoicing/refund systems, and criminal penalties (including imprisonment and fines) may be imposed for fraudulent invoices/export documentation; the tax authority's reopening/claw-back powers generally cover the statutory inspection years under Egyptian tax law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole monetary, foreign-exchange, banking-licensing and payment-systems regulator for the Arab Republic of Egypt, acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 promulgating the Central Bank and Banking System Law, as amended, together with the Exchange Control Law regime, the Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, and the Payment Systems and Electronic Money Law No. 18 of 2019.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP operates under managed-float status and is convertible for current-transaction purposes under an IMF Article VIII orientation; however, Egypt is not a fully capital-account liberalised jurisdiction. Commercial banks receive current-account transfers with standard documentary support, but capital transactions—foreign equity contribution into an Egyptian LLC, shareholder loans, treasury derivatives, profit repatriation and liquidation proceeds—must be channelled through a CBE-authorised dealer bank and are subject to administrative controls, beneficial-ownership verification, tax clearance and statistical reporting. Profit remittance hurdles for a non-resident shareholder arise at execution points: audited local financial statements and tax clearance must exist, distributable reserves must satisfy the Company Law solvency test, and the remitting bank will require a signed board resolution, dividend declaration and a Form C remittance application before actual transfer. Since 2016 there is no legal dual exchange rate; conversion occurs at the interbank or bank-offered rate. The CBE may, during exigencies, activate temporary prioritisation rules or directed order for conversion, but as of Q1 2025 it has not imposed a general surrendered-conversion ratio on export proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE export-proceeds regulations implementing the Exchange Control Law, an Egyptian LLC exporter must repatriate to Egypt 100% of the value of goods shipped through an authorised bank within five (5) months from the date of the bill of lading or transport document; late receipt requires prior CBE approval or creates a default under the authorised bank's export documentation submission. The statutory conversion ratio to EGP is not fixed at 100%: the exporter may retain the full proceeds in a foreign-currency account (FCA) or convert them to EGP at the prevailing market/interbank rate. For the hydroponics e-commerce exporter, proceeds collected by Stripe or PayPal are treated as export receipts only when settled from the PSP settlement wallet to an Egyptian bank account in the exporter's name; such receipts must be identified in the bank's monthly foreign-currency report and attached to the export customs forms to avoid re-invoicing and transfer-pricing challenges.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational EGP/FCY Account
Capital Escrow Account and E-Merchant Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational EGP/FCY Account
Operational EGP/FCY Account with E-commerce Acquiring Support
Operational EGP/FCY Account and Trade-Clearing Desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a standalone primary treasury rail; Medium as a complementary payment sub-acquirer. CBE Law No. 18 of 2019 requires any entity providing electronic-money services or cross-border payments in Egypt to hold a CBE e-money institution licence or operate through a licensed bank. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut and Payoneer cannot open corporate EGP bank accounts or hold clearing/settlement accounts directly with the CBE; for an Egyptian LLC they may act only as an unregulated facilitator or route through an authorised PSP. The recommended treasury infrastructure is to use Stripe and PayPal as front-end e-commerce PSPs, settle into a CBE-licensed bank account via local commercial acquirers, and keep all FX conversion with the Egyptian authorised dealer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required for the corporate legal representative and each authorised signatory at the time of account opening. The LLC's manager or managing director and all individual beneficial owners with a direct or indirect interest of 25% or more must attend an in-branch KYC interview; remote opening for non-resident-owned LLCs is not accepted on a standard CBE-compliant basis. Directors located outside Egypt may give a general power-of-attorney to a resident authorised signatory, but the UBO's identity and source-of-funds evidence must still be presented in the original or apostilled/consular-certified copy, and a remote video call is treated only as supplementary verification, not as a replacement for the in-branch interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Electronic-commerce cross-border PSP inflows with no clean corresponding invoice trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PSP merchant agreement and settlement statement; order-level sales ledger with customer identification, shipping and tracking numbers and delivery confirmations; applicable VAT and e-invoice records; warehouse or fulfilment contracts; and a funds-flow narrative describing how receipts reconcile to export sales of hydroponics equipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or UBO located in a jurisdiction considered by Egyptian banks to have weak AML or sanctions controls
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copy; proof-of-address statement; corporate registry abstract for entity shareholders; consolidated sanctions and PEP screening output from CBE-recognised databases; notarised wealth-source declaration using letters from banks, audited financial statements or sale contracts; and a statement of structure from each UBO with no shell or nominee ambiguity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of substantive physical or operational substance in Egypt while booking sales through the LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial Registry certificate showing the registered address; GAFI investment certificate for the LLC; lease or usufruct agreement for office or warehouse; utility bills; payroll returns to the Egyptian Tax Authority; logistics and inventory-holding records; and audited or internally prepared financial projections proving actual business activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-currency capital contribution inconsistent with the registered share capital or paid-in capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity's Articles of Association as approved by GAFI; CBE bank inward remittance registration; a bank advice from the remitting shareholder with purpose code; board or shareholder resolution approving the capital call; proof of transfer fees or taxes paid; and audited financials or bank reference showing the lawful source of the funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple lines of business or future freight-forwarding or trade mixture triggering payment-float concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated ISIC and NEC listing in the Commercial Registry; supplier due-diligence pack for all vendors; transaction monitoring programme; local tax authority registration; and a counterparty list showing no prohibited dual-use or agricultural-quota goods beyond the hydroponics equipment scope.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders' cash equity injections must be transferred only by SWIFT to the LLC's capital suspense or operational account at a CBE-authorised dealer bank using MT103, or MT202 for bank-to-bank credit inside the same network. The remittance advice must state the ultimate remitter, the Egyptian beneficiary TIN, and the purpose narrative 'Capital subscription to EG LLC under the Egyptian Investment Law'; the bank will record the transaction in the balance-of-payments statistical register and issue an inward invoice or contract form. The applicable BPM6 purpose code is DI3, direct-investment equity other than reinvested earnings. The funds may be held in the original foreign currency or sold for EGP at the reference or interbank rate, but cannot be settled out of the country: every wire must be cleared via the CBE RTGS and each bank will require a foreign-currency account instruction and the company's current commercial registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For purchase of hydroponics equipment and spare parts, the LLC should use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for low-value suppliers, documentary commercial import letters of credit through an Egyptian opening bank for high-value equipment with MT700 and MT710 issuance and advice, and MT202 cover payments for bank-side reimbursement. Import settlements must be registered with the CBE-authorised bank on the import documentary form and supported by proforma invoices, customs declarations, insurance certificates and GOEIC import registration, as applicable; payment in EGP is permissible for domestic suppliers. The company's PSP sweep from PayPal or Stripe should be batched daily into the Egyptian settlement account; the sweep is not an outbound trade disbursement but must be evidenced as current-account export settlement within the same bank relationship.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable EGP/USD foreign-currency forwards with a confirmed export or import transaction as the underlying economic exposure, contract tenors generally up to 12 months
FX swaps between EGP and USD, EUR or trade currencies executed with a CBE-authorised dealer, used to reposition liquidity on settlement dates
Cross-currency swaps for shareholder-loan or equipment-finance liabilities, provided the transaction is approved by the CBE and documented as a hedging derivative and not a speculative position

Forward-hedging of PSP revenue streams through the bank's own treasury line, supported by the PSP settlement forecast and the merchant acquiring agreement; NDFs are not a permitted onshore Egyptian bank clearing product, but an offshore counterparty may hold a mirroring NDF only outside the onshore clearing system

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, late-payment interest, tax examination, and assessment risks apply. Persistent non-compliance may result in administrative enforcement and license or registration consequences; no universal automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and corporate accounts approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, where filing is required, and the company's partners' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements should be prepared after financial year-end and submitted to the ordinary partners' meeting generally within three months after year-end, subject to the company's accounting period and applicable Companies Law requirements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines, notices, inspection, suspension of company services, and potential dissolution or strike-off proceedings may follow material or persistent non-compliance. No single automatic strike-off deadline applies to all Egyptian LLCs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary partners' meeting and approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company partners; resolutions and prescribed filings are maintained or submitted through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the end of the financial year, unless a different lawful timing applies under the company's constitutional documents or regulatory requirements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting may impair approval of accounts, distributions, and management discharge and may lead to GAFI notices, administrative penalties, and escalation for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate file, manager, partner, and constitutional amendment update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not an annual filing; submit promptly following any change in partners, managers, capital, registered address, business purpose, or constitutional documents, subject to the applicable filing period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered changes may be unenforceable against third parties and may result in administrative fines, rejection of subsequent filings, suspension of services, and possible dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership and ownership-control information review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records maintained for competent Egyptian authorities; relevant information may be requested by GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, or AML authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Review at least annually and update promptly after any change in ownership, control, or beneficial ownership; no generally applicable annual public UBO confirmation statement is prescribed for an ordinary Egyptian LLC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or produce accurate beneficial ownership information may trigger AML enforcement, administrative penalties, enhanced scrutiny, and restrictions on corporate or banking services.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent auditor is generally required for Egyptian companies governed by the Companies Law where statutory conditions apply, including specified capital, partner-number, or constitutional-document thresholds. The exact obligation should be confirmed against the current Companies Law, the company's capital, partner count, and articles. A company within the audit regime must appoint a licensed Egyptian auditor and submit audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards, with IFRS-based requirements and Egyptian statutory adaptations; tax reporting follows Egyptian tax law and Egyptian Tax Authority requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is generally no separate annual UBO confirmation filing for an ordinary Egyptian LLC. The company should conduct an annual ownership and control review, maintain accurate beneficial ownership records, and update its corporate and AML records promptly following any share transfer or control change. Share transfers require compliance with the company's articles, Companies Law formalities, and applicable GAFI authentication or registration procedures.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of partners' meetings and management resolutions
Register of Beneficial Owners and ownership-control information
Accounting books, supporting records, and approved annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,000 per year, depending on location, mail handling, local representative services, and filing support; Egypt does not generally require a separate annual registered-agent renewal fee for an ordinary LLC.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,500-6,000 for a small Egyptian LLC with ordinary transactions; higher fees apply to substantial revenue, inventory, foreign ownership, multiple payment channels, or complex reporting.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket exemption for e-commerce retail. Preferential tax holidays under Law 72/2017 apply only to qualifying industrial/agricultural investment zones; standard LLCs incur a flat 22.5% CIT on worldwide profits because the former defense/national-security surtaxes were integrated into the headline rate in 2020 (Law 26/2020).
